en: Points of Controversy,
Great Chapter,
Sixteenth Section.
The Discourse on Whether Form is With Cause: Is form with cause? Yes.
“Is it caused by non-greed?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Is it caused by non-hatred? …pe…
By way of the cause of non-delusion … [and so on] … by way of the cause of greed … [and so on] … by way of the cause of hatred … [and so on] …
Is it because of delusion?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is material form accompanied by a cause?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does it have an object? Is there its turning toward [the object] … down to … its aspiration?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
But is it not the case that it has no object, and for it there is no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration?
Yes, you say.
If it has no object, and for it there is no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration, then indeed, sir, you should not say: [that it is consciousness].
“Form has a cause.
Is non-greed with a cause and an object, and does it have turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration? Yes.
"Is material form (rūpa) accompanied by a cause (sahetuka) and possessed of an object (sārammaṇa)? Is there for it turning toward [the object] …pe… aspiration (paṇidhi)?
One should not say so …pe… "Is non-hatred (adosa) accompanied by a cause …pe…"? One should not say so.
Non-delusion … faith … energy …
Mindfulness … concentration … wisdom …
Greed … hatred … delusion …
conceit … views … doubt …
Sloth … restlessness … lack of moral shame …
Is fearlessness of wrongdoing (anottappa) accompanied by a cause (sahetuka) and possessed of an object (sārammaṇa), and does it have turning toward [the object]... up to ...
aspiration (paṇidhi)? Yes. Is material form (rūpa) accompanied by a cause and possessed of an object, and does it have turning toward... up to ... aspiration? No.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Matter is with cause but without an object; there is no turning toward it … [as before] … nor aspiration? Yes.
Is non-greed (alobha) accompanied by a cause but without an object, such that it has no turning toward [objects], nor aspiration, and so forth?
One should not say so...
Is material form (rūpa) accompanied by a cause but without an object, such that it has no turning toward [objects], nor aspiration, and so forth?
“Yes.
“Is non-hatred with a cause?
… [and so on] … Is non-shame with a cause but without an object, and does it lack turning toward, … [and so on] … aspiration?”
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Should it not be stated that “material form is with cause”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that form has conditions?
“Yes.”
If matter is conditioned, then indeed, O friend, it must be said that "matter has a cause.
The discussion on the thesis that matter has a cause is finished.
